title: The Aliasing Trap
goal: Avoid mutating a collection while holding a reference to an element.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 2 Morning: Borrow Checking

hints: i32 implements Copy, so reading a primitive number by value copies it and ends any borrow.
Holding a reference like &nums[0] across nums.push() causes E0502 when the reference is used later.
explanation: Assigning `nums[0]` directly copies the `i32` value into `val`, so no borrow of `nums` remains active when `nums.push()` is called. Using `&nums[0]` or `nums.get(0)` creates a shared reference that lingers until `println!("{val}")`, causing `E0502` when `nums.push()` attempts a mutable borrow. Calling `*val` on `i32` fails with `E0614` because primitive integers cannot be dereferenced. Calling `.unwrap()` on `i32` or `&i32` fails with `E0599` because they lack an `unwrap` method. Multiplying `Option<&i32>` directly fails with `E0369`.
